title: GPU-accelerated wind farm layout search with a distilled endogenous wake model (EndoWake)
contribution: Distills the EndoWake MILP field model into a GPU batch evaluator and uses it as a screen in front of a trusted wake model (screen-and-confirm), showing that fidelity is not decision quality and that throughput pays only when the search is built for it (pp. 1, 3-4).
problem_entry: Wind farm layout under award conditions; wake computation is the bottleneck (RANS 405 s per direction); entry via the authors' own EndoWake MILP, framed by the optimizer's curse (pp. 1-3).
key_idea: Distillation of four EndoWake parameters (closed-form amplitude, eq. (7), p. 10), GPU batch evaluation at 1,093,103 layouts/s (pp. 8, 12), and screen-and-confirm with list length L = ceil(q rP/rE) from measured rates (pp. 20-21).
assumptions: Binary site-selection MILP with propagation inequalities, big-M wake source, SOS2 power curve (B = 8), clique separation (pp. 7-8); finite-support kernel, no blockage/shear/veer, kernel tied to cell size and turbulence (pp. 10, 12); Lillgrund and Horns Rev 1 data (pp. 9, 16, 26).
proof_devices: concave-envelope dual bound, proved in technical note (p. 13)
experiments: Side-constraint and industrial-size runs (pp. 14-15); RANS-judged Lillgrund bench with phase test (pp. 15-19); 5 development + 20 unseen frozen seeds: +4.28% in 38 s vs +4.33% in 294 s, 7.9x (certified 3.0x), AEP 14.9x; Horns Rev 1 0.29 points below; speed-up decomposed (pp. 20-27, 33-34).
positioning: Table 1 places it among approximate/accelerated evaluation methods; precedents of multi-fidelity preselection credited, claim limited to their combination; spatially localized surrogate bias claimed as new (pp. 3, 5-6).
writing: Roles defined before experiments (p. 9); 'RANS reference' not 'CFD' (p. 10); inherited-vs-new paragraph (p. 3); hedges at the claim (pp. 14, 17, 19); dropped colourful name (p. 15); original draft by Martina Fischetti, weak evidence of his voice (p. 28).
limits_future: One site, one RANS inflow and speed, farm power not AEP (p. 27); not faster than PyWake at equal hardware (pp. 12-13); Horns Rev 1 shortfall (p. 27); corrected earlier implementation error (pp. 10, 30); future: speed-dependent reduction factor, judge outside RANS, lidar transects (pp. 27-28).

title: Just sort it! A note on the LP behind rank-one anti-loop edits
contribution: Shows that on this model the sparse LP inside the AHA rank-one anti-loop edit can be replaced by a sort of neurons by coefficient of variation within a pre-declared non-inferiority margin, with the dose even taken from AHA's delta without any LP (p. 3).
problem_entry: Is the LP of the AHA weight edit needed? Entry by measuring the LP (12,000 rows, ~43M nonzeros, ~2.2 min, very sparse optima) and reading its solution as a bias along u rather than a separation (pp. 1-2, 4).
key_idea: Replace the solve by a sort: k = 8 neurons with smallest sigma_j/|m_j|, v_j = c/(k m_j) with the dose borrowed from the LP (sort_k8); controls knap_k8 and sortd_k8 with AHA's delta (pp. 2-3).
assumptions: MILP forms n/a; LP with L1 objective and slacks, then restriction to 8 neurons and re-solve (p. 1); exploits near-constant always-active neurons (p. 2); Qwen3.5-0.8B, MATH-500 and 500 GSM8K, one sample per problem (p. 2); no correctness argument (p. 2).
experiments: Unmodified AHA at commit e6e94ff5, protocol and 5-point margin declared before runs; seed 0: LP 67.4% vs sort_k8 67.0% (-0.4 [-2.9, +2.1]); second protocol on three new seeds: sort_k8 -0.6 [-2.0, +0.8], sortd_k8 -0.8, knap_k8 -0.9; steering control not run (pp. 2-3).
positioning: Only AHA [1] and Barry's LP [2] discussed; no literature on activation steering or sparse LP (pp. 1-4).
writing: Imperative title, numbers in abstract; falsified first reading as the turn (pp. 1-2); wording calibrated to the missing control (p. 3); prose written by the AI assistant, no evidence of his voice (p. 4).
limits_future: One model, one run of the pipeline producing u, seeds measure sampling only, steering control missing and named next (pp. 2-3); artifacts on Zenodo (p. 4).

title: A Dantzig-Wolfe reformulation of the EndoWake model for optimal wind farm layouts
contribution: A Dantzig-Wolfe reformulation on enumerated tiles, a cube-of-speed coordinate that makes the second stage concave, and master shrinking certify every EndoWake ladder grid up to 16x16 and a pre-specified unseen test set where the earlier branch-and-check fails (pp. 4, 20).
problem_entry: Certification is hard: weak LP relaxation, published branch-and-check leaves 12x12-16x16 at 7.98-9.74% gaps and its bound stays 7.3% above optimum even with optimal cutoff; question is how far a certificate can be pushed by tile convexification (p. 2).
key_idea: Tiles of b = 4 at stride 2 enumerated as DW columns with linking x (eq. (9), Prop. 3, pp. 8-10); cube coordinate q = (w/V)^3 linearizes power and makes the field concave, enabling generalized Benders cuts (pp. 6-7); reduced-cost fixing, pairwise consistency propagation, refixing (pp. 11-12).
assumptions: n x n grid, 3D separation, at most n+2 turbines, four axial directions at 10 m/s, cubic power curve, calibrated kernel (pp. 4-5); Proposition 1 restated (p. 5); cut-in transfer checked on 153 layouts as evidence not proof; epsilon = 1e-6 shift is a relaxation (pp. 6-7); valid for antitone fields (p. 18).
proof_devices: induction along propagation planes (Proposition 1, p. 5; Proposition 2, p. 7)
quasi-concavity plus positive homogeneity for concavity of the power mean (Lemma 1, p. 6)
concavity-against-antitonicity sandwich for the exact upwind cut (Lemma 2, p. 8)
LP duality for column fixing with a moving incumbent, plus propagation validity (Proposition 4, Appendix A, p. 21)
antitonicity validity of the tile block (Proposition 3, pp. 9-10)
experiments: Frozen 2026a branch-and-check baseline on same hardware and gurobipy 13.0.3 (pp. 13-14); 5 seeds, medians, censored runs excluded (pp. 14-15); ladder all certified vs 0/5 above 10x10 (p. 15); 78/78 roses (p. 16); 16x16 5/5 (p. 16); attribution (p. 17); 36-instance unseen test set 106/108 vs 38/108 (pp. 17-18); failures at twelve directions and 17x17 (pp. 19-20).
positioning: Each ingredient's precedent credited (Gilmore-Gomory, DW, arrowhead, local cuts, route enumeration, reduced-cost filtering, consistency cuts, generalized/logic Benders); novelty in their combination, cube coordinate claimed as new (pp. 3-4).
writing: Abstract defines 'certified' and medians (p. 1); plain admissions (pp. 2, 20); Benders cut as cleaner equivalent not speed-up (p. 8); hypothesis labelled (p. 19); floating-point certificates (p. 14); AI-assisted drafting, original draft by Martina Fischetti (pp. 22-23).
limits_future: Tight only on axial wakes (pp. 19-20); 17x17 open, memory limits (p. 19); no safe bound (p. 14); one instance family (p. 3); future: column-generated root, stronger direction coupling, pricing in the tree (pp. 19-20).

transferable: When the relaxation is weak, enumerate the patterns of small overlapping substructures and add them as Dantzig–Wolfe columns; validity needs only a monotonicity (antitone) property, exactness a cut at integer points (pp. 8–10).
Look for the coordinate in which the value function becomes concave (here the cube of the speed), so a generalized Benders cut with a supergradient from one reverse sweep becomes available (pp. 6–7).

With an incumbent at or near the optimum, fix columns by root reduced costs (v + c̄ < L), propagate pairwise consistency between overlapping blocks, and refix at every improving incumbent with lazy λ ≤ 0 where bounds cannot change in a callback (pp. 11–12, 21).
Pass the incumbent as a complete MIP start, continuous variables included at their exact values, or lazy cuts reject it (p. 11).
Compare design variants with the same incumbent and on deterministic work units when machines differ (pp. 10, 14).

Run the published baseline frozen and as published, then once more with the optimum as cutoff to measure the proof effort alone (pp. 14–16).
Generate a held-out test set from a seed fixed before any run, varying what the development ladder kept fixed (masks, budgets, roses), and run each code once (p. 17).
Score candidates in low precision on a GPU but accept only after an exact double-precision re-evaluation of the top few (p. 13).

quotes.text: These are the certificates of a floating-point solver: we compute no safe bound in the sense of Neumaier and Shcherbina (2004), and the width is the margin we report.

The instances of the ladder are those on which the pipeline was developed. To measure what it does on instances it has not seen, we generated a test set of 36 instances from a seed fixed before any run, and ran both codes on it once.

title: Minibatch persistency, eight years later: what batch reuse costs in steps and joules, and what it saves in data
contribution: A pre-registered, tuned re-test of his own 2018 minibatch-persistency claim, measuring cost on steps, fresh tokens and joules against an A/A null, which finds that reuse buys data, not speed or energy, and only at large batch (pp. 1-2).
problem_entry: Entry from the standing objection of Choi et al. (2019) that the 2018 study tuned nothing; conceded and sharpened (K steps at eta resemble one at K*eta); plus no joule measurements existed (pp. 1-2).
key_idea: Knobs K and M; arms baseline, persistency (K=4, M=1) and A/A null (K=4, M=4 resample) (pp. 4-5); paired step-cost ratio R(B,s), H1 g(512) < g(32) with a registered three-outcome rule (p. 6); rho(B) diagnostic (pp. 2, 8).
assumptions: MILP items n/a; 49M-parameter Transformer, AdamW, cosine schedule, only peak rate tuned (pp. 5, 7); FineWeb-Edu pre-tokenized, fixed evaluation set, 100 Mtok per run (p. 7); exchangeability not verified (p. 5); arms read at different schedule points (pp. 5, 7); model cut by Amendment 1 (p. 7).
proof_devices: identity fresh-token ratio = R/K at M = 1 (p. 6)
evaluation-grid offset (K-1)/t verified seed by seed (pp. 23-24)
bound placing host-inclusive energy ratio between device-joule and seconds ratios (p. 12)
experiments: OSF pre-registration with signed tags and amendments, interim looks disclosed (pp. 8-9, 16, 29); 144 primary runs: g(32) = 2.886 vs g(512) = 0.4190, p = 9.8e-10, supported (pp. 14-16); A/A ratios contain one (p. 16); replication on seeds 8-15 (pp. 18-20); schedule-matched control E3 not separable (pp. 21-22); epoch contrast (p. 27); 477 runs on free-tier GPUs (pp. 7, 10).
positioning: Tuned-baseline (Shallue et al.; Kaddour et al.; AlgoPerf) and device-energy traditions (p. 4); Choi et al.'s equal tuning adopted at smaller budget, noted as unrefereed (p. 3); no mechanism novelty claimed (p. 3); theory line not citing 2018/2019 work (pp. 3-4); EU AI Act Annex XI (p. 4).
writing: Abstract leads with the outcome (p. 1); inconvenient facts announced in place (pp. 9, 15, 21, 22, 24); halves read together (p. 27); lesson learned at the end (p. 28); figure kept to forestall the 2018 criticism (p. 23).
limits_future: Budget-limited small model, one dataset (pp. 7-8); K = 4 only, strict reuse only, no locality claim (pp. 4-5, 29); rho indeterminate at B = 512 (p. 14); host energy excluded (p. 12); archive on acceptance, OSF embargoed to 2027-08-10 (p. 29); future: locality, vision arm, decorated reuse, scale, second K, theory bridge (p. 29).
